@chliny2016 

V2.2.5, which always includes Allowed NSSAI in Registration accept, will be up soon. I don't know if this can solve your problem.

The following is the content of the standard document.
```
    /*
     * TS24.501
     *
     * 4.6.2 Mobility management aspects
     * 4.6.2.1 General
     *
     * The UE in NB-N1 mode does not include the requested NSSAI during
     * the registration procedure if the 5GS registration type IE indicates
     * "mobility registration updating", procedure is not initiated
     * to change the slice(s) that the UE is currently registered to,
     * and the UE is still in the current registration area. The AMF does not
     * include the allowed NSSAI during a registration procedure with the 5GS
     * registration type IE indicating "mobility registration updating" except
     * if the allowed NSSAI has changed for the UE. The UE considers
     * the last received allowed NSSAI as valid until the UE receives
     * a new allowed NSSAI.
     *
     * 5.5.1.2.4 Initial registration accepted by the network
     *
     * The AMF shall include the allowed NSSAI for the current PLMN
     * and shall include the mapped S-NSSAI(s) for the allowed NSSAI
     * contained in the requested NSSAI from the UE if available,
     * in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message if the UE included
     * the requested NSSAI in the REGISTRATION REQUEST message
     * and the AMF allows one or more S-NSSAIs in the requested NSSAI.
     */
```

Basically, I don't think there is a need to send an Allowed NSSAI if there is no requested NSSAI in the registration request (with mobility registration update) and if this has not been modified by AMF.

However, the standard document describes only the UE in NB-N1 mode. There is no content for WB-N1 mode.

I'm not sure that I can skip an Allowed NSSAI. Therefore, I do not optimize this part, and I will always send Allowed NSSAI at this point.

Let me know if you have any further questions.

Thank you so much for your effort.
Sukchan

I think GUTI is not the issue. If it was, UE coldn't use old GUTI in mobility registration. There is 2 possible error it can cause mobility registration.
1-UE sends ims session request even its data centric. I think this is about imsVops parameter in register accept. UE may trigger ims session when it receives this parameter as supported. AMF should check whether UE support imsVops or not then send this parameter as supported.
2- UPF does not response gtp packets. When UE does not get response to GTP packets, it can trigger mobility registration

But if you didn't see this problem with older versions, its probably second reason. If you check UPF configs and data can be transferred to UE over UPF, I think you dont meet with  this problem again.

I've reviewed the presence of GUTI between v2.1.7 and current version, but there is no difference. It doesn't seem to be a problem with the presence of the 5G-GUTI.
